chapter_summaries.summary: Lockwood narrates his first visit to Wuthering Heights in 1801. He meets his landlord, Mr. Heathcliff, whose reserved and suspicious manner fascinates him. After entering the bleak, old house and noting its strange architecture, furnishings, and the name Hareton Earnshaw carved above the door, Lockwood reflects at length on Heathcliff’s character and on his own awkwardness in human relations. Left briefly alone, he attempts to pet a dog and provokes a violent attack from several of the house dogs, until a kitchen woman intervenes. Heathcliff responds with brusque indifference, then offers wine and becomes somewhat more civil. Despite clear signs that Heathcliff does not welcome company, Lockwood decides he will visit again.
